title: Sampling-date spread gave no clear change in moth richness warmth slopes in four British samples in 1992-2015
abstract: We tested whether sampling-date spread changed monthly warmth slopes for moth richness at equal catch size. We used 685 trap-months from England and Scotland in 1992-2003 and 2004-2015. Models controlled trap by month, rain, sample count, mean sample date and time. Adding date spread changed warmth slopes by -0.049 to +0.101 taxa per C. All four corrected intervals included zero. All four date-spread slope intervals also included zero. Residual date spread varied little, especially in Scotland. Thus the result does not show that sampling calendars have no effect. Few year clusters, coarse weather, selected complete months and shared monitoring records limit inference. This follow-up reuses observations from earlier campaign work. It tests no pollution or causal climate effect. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and a figure support inspection. Raw inputs and derived record tables remain external.

display.caption: Date-spread slopes, adjusted warmth slopes and paired warmth slope changes. Bars are four-test intervals. Each panel has separate units.
